# Example Data Repository

> Public studies of human immune response. Each study has an HTML page, a Markdown alternate, a schema.org Dataset record in JSON-LD, and a citation. Study identifiers look like SDY1001.

This file is the reading order for an agent. It is a demonstration for the 6 November 2026 NIAID Blueprint webinar and is not served at `/llms.txt`. Replace `example.org` before publishing it.

The sitemap at <https://example.org/sitemap.xml> is the inventory. It lists public URLs and the `lastmod` of each page, and it can name a bulk file. This file names what to read, in what order, and why. It stays small enough to fit in context. The detail sits behind the links.

Crawl permission is in <https://example.org/robots.txt>. Search and user-triggered fetch are allowed there. Training crawls are not. A page that is disallowed is not listed here.

Read the Markdown alternate of a page. The HTML is for a person, and its text may appear only after JavaScript runs. Two URL shapes are both valid. A page at `/about/citation.html` can publish `/about/citation.html.md` (the suffix appended). A page at `/docs/access.html` can publish `/docs/access.md` (the extension replaced). A directory URL appends `index.md` or `index.html.md`.

The page points at that Markdown and at the `llms.txt` that covers it. Use an HTML `link` element, or a `Link` header. The header also works on the Markdown file and on a file that is not HTML, and a CDN can add it without editing the page. Some servers also honor `Accept: text/markdown`. The link relation is the discovery path to rely on.

```
Link: </studies/SDY1001.md>; rel="alternate"; type="text/markdown", </studies/llms.txt>; rel="describedby"
```

```html
<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="https://example.org/studies/SDY1001.md">
<link rel="describedby" href="https://example.org/studies/llms.txt">
```

An `llms.txt` covers the pages under its own path. This file covers the site. A file at `/studies/llms.txt` covers `/studies/`, and the more specific file wins for those pages. The Optional section is secondary reading. Skip it when the context is short. The name carries no other parser rule.

Links may leave this host. A sitemap cannot do that.

## Start here

- [Repository overview](https://example.org/index.md): What the repository holds, and what an agent can cite.
- [Citation](https://example.org/about/citation.html.md): The citation string and the BibTeX for a study. Markdown suffix appended to the HTML name.
- [Access and licenses](https://example.org/docs/access.md): Which studies are open, and which require an agreement. Extension replaced with `.md`.

## Studies

- [Study guide](https://example.org/studies/llms.txt): The `llms.txt` for `/studies/`. Use it instead of this file for a study page.
- [Study index](https://example.org/studies/index.md): How study pages, identifiers, and files are laid out. Directory form of the Markdown URL.
- [SDY1001](https://example.org/studies/SDY1001.md): One current study, in Markdown. The HTML page is <https://example.org/studies/SDY1001>.
- [SDY1001 JSON-LD](https://example.org/studies/SDY1001?format=jsonld&profile=niaid): The same study as a schema.org Dataset record.

## API and bulk

- [OpenAPI description](https://example.org/api/openapi.yaml): Operations, parameters, and the JSON-LD media type.
- [API skill](https://example.org/api/skills/niaid-records/SKILL.md): The steps an agent follows to call the records API.
- [Study package, October 2026](https://example.org/download/studies-2026-10.zip): One transfer of the public studies. The sitemap lists each package and its `lastmod`.

## Optional

- [NIAID Blueprint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/go-fair-us/ai-blueprint-core/refs/heads/master/docs/BluePrint/NIAID_Blueprint_v2_26Sep2025_forExternal.md): Metadata, identifier, API, and citation practices this repository follows. This URL is on another host.
- [Glossary](https://example.org/docs/glossary.md): Terms used on the study pages.
- [Archived study SDY0042](https://example.org/studies/SDY0042.md)
